upstream.adaptation: Retains the single upstream PlayerSavegame saved-field owner, adapting its table boundary to the selected local SkillTables API. Character PropertyState, runtime inventory and profile lifecycle are not copied into this owner.

functions.role: Initializes one saved-skill row for each selected Character SkillList member, initially level zero.
Updates an existing saved skill level.
Reads a saved level by selected-list index.
Writes a skill-slot mapping and calls the supplied skill-update boundary.
Reads the named Skills profile section against the selected SkillList and slot maps.
Empty argument vector appends nothing; otherwise reads/converts the argument, scans selected SkillList OIDs, and appends the matching index or -1.
Empty arguments or an out-of-range selected-list index append nothing; a valid index validates the SkillTable member and appends the saved level, with a null save owner yielding -1.
Negative or out-of-range SkillTree selector uses SkillList row 3.
Resolves the selected source SkillList row.
Returns the first matching SkillList member index, or -1.
Resolves and validates the selected SkillList member against SkillTables before saved-level lookup.
Forwards the index to the Character's save owner, returning -1 for null.

local_scope.owner: PlayerSavegameV1 owns saved fields and zero-initialized skill levels; current SkillTree and SkillTables are borrowed. Invalid selector fallback is the real empty row 3.
local_scope.callbacks: The borrowed callback adapters in player_savegame_v1.hpp use the current PropertyView and SkillTables. Current-info validates that the save owner identity matches the invoking Character; this is an adapter binding guard, while the source obtains the pointer from Character+0x14e8.
not_reconstructed: Starter skill grants or nonzero skill levels
Character Lua Value conversion/Argument vector Invoke ABI
Native Player lifecycle ownership; the caller must retain this single owner through script calls

evidence.host_scope: Source save-owner differential replay plus real-cache selector/callback guards; callback wrappers themselves are pinned to recovered ARM functions, not run as a second native ABI emulator.
